name: Photo / video integration
controls: Whether and how real photography, live-action footage and screenshots enter the motion graphic, and how graphics relate to them (framed, masked, composited, tracked).
question: Should real photos, footage or screenshots appear, and how are they combined with the graphics?
notes: Photo and video integration ranges from none (fully graphic) through framed media (footage inside a card, device or UI) to composited media (masked, cut out, tracked). The integration choice sets how 'real' the piece feels: full-bleed and documentary footage read as authentic and human; framed and floating media read as product and interface; masked and cut-out media read as editorial and designed. In HyperFrames, footage is placed as video elements whose playback the framework owns (do not call play() or set currentTime yourself); graphics animate around or over them with GSAP, and masks use CSS clip-path, mask-image or SVG masks on the media's wrapper. True motion tracking and screen replacement require source data (tracking points or corner pins exported from a tracker) or footage shot for it; without that, simulate with locked-off or slowly pushed shots where graphics move with a matching tween. Photo cutouts need a background-removed PNG/WebP (media-use can remove backgrounds). Combinations are common: full-bleed footage plus photo typography, device mockup plus floating screenshots, cutouts plus doodles.

options.what: No photography or footage; every pixel is designed graphics, type, UI or illustration.
options.looks: Vector shapes, type, UI and illustration only; full control of color and composition.
options.motion: All motion is authored; no source timing to respect.
options.use: Most SaaS launch films, explainers, kinetic typography, logo stings, data films.
options.conveys: Designed clarity, brand control, abstraction.
options.vs: Illustrative approaches can imitate photography; 'none' means no photographic source at all.
options.prompt: Use no photography, footage or screenshots: build every visual from type, vector shapes, recreated UI and illustration in the defined palette, so color, lighting and timing are fully controlled.

options.what: Live-action video fills the entire frame edge to edge, with graphics layered on top.
options.looks: Cinematic footage filling 16:9 or 9:16, typography and lower-thirds overlaid, grade unified with brand.
options.motion: Footage carries the motion; graphics enter with restraint; cuts on action.
options.use: Brand films, campaign ads, event recaps, social ads.
options.conveys: Authenticity, emotion, the real world.
options.vs: Footage inside frames shows video as an object in a designed layout; full-bleed makes footage the world.
options.prompt: Fill the frame with the footage (object-fit cover, no borders), apply a unifying grade overlay (a 10-20% brand-color multiply or a gradient scrim at the bottom for legibility), and keep overlaid type to one or two lines placed in the shot's negative space.

options.what: Video plays inside designed shapes (rounded cards, circles, grid cells) within a graphic layout.
options.looks: Rounded-rectangle or arch-shaped video windows on a flat background, sometimes several at once.
options.motion: Frames move, resize and rearrange while the footage plays inside; frames can expand to full-bleed.
options.use: Product films, social promos, brand content mixing people and UI, testimonials.
options.conveys: Curated, designed, human but controlled.
options.vs: Masked video uses type or complex shapes as the window; footage in frames uses simple layout containers.
options.prompt: Place footage in layout containers with overflow hidden and a consistent radius (24-48px) or arch shape, object-fit cover; animate the containers (position, size, radius) rather than the video, and let one frame expand to full-bleed at the key moment.

options.what: Video appears as content within an interface: a video call, a media player, a feed post, a thumbnail.
options.looks: Recreated UI chrome (player controls, chat panels, call grids) with live footage in the content area.
options.motion: UI interactions (play, scrub, pin) with footage playing within.
options.use: Video, collaboration and social products; creator tools; communication apps.
options.conveys: Real usage, human presence in the product.
options.vs: Picture-in-picture is a small inset over another view; footage in UI is content integral to the interface.
options.prompt: Recreate the interface in HTML (player chrome, call grid tiles, feed card) and place footage in its content slots with object-fit cover; animate UI state changes (speaker highlight ring, captions appearing, controls fading) around the playing video.

options.what: Footage is visible only through a shape or typography mask.
options.looks: Giant letters filled with moving footage; a logo silhouette with video inside.
options.motion: The mask scales, moves or expands to reveal full footage; video plays inside the shape.
options.use: Title cards, brand films, event openers, editorial.
options.conveys: Designed boldness, brand and reality fused.
options.vs: Footage in frames uses layout containers; masked video uses the shape of type or logo as the window.
options.prompt: Show footage only through a mask: apply an SVG mask or CSS mask-image of heavy display type (900 weight, set huge) or the logo to the video wrapper; animate the mask's scale from 1 to 20-40 to expand into full-bleed footage at the payoff.

options.what: Multiple video clips play simultaneously in a grid or free-form arrangement.
options.looks: Bento grids or overlapping tiles of different clips, sometimes mixed with type cards.
options.motion: Tiles cascade in, reorganize, one expands; rhythmic swaps of clips within tiles.
options.use: Community and creator products, event recaps, brand anthems, social.
options.conveys: Abundance, diversity, energy, a community.
options.vs: Footage in frames usually features one or two windows; a collage is a multitude.
options.prompt: Arrange 4-12 clips in a bento or free grid with 8-16px gutters, cascade tiles in with the motion language's enter ease, swap clips inside tiles on beats, and end by expanding one tile to full frame while the others exit.

options.what: Photographic subjects isolated from their background and placed on graphic backgrounds.
options.looks: People or products cut out cleanly (sometimes with a white sticker border) against flat color or collage.
options.motion: Cutouts pop, slide or scale as rigid objects; puppet-like limb moves; drop shadows follow.
options.use: Collage styles, social promos, editorial, youth brands, mixed-media explainers.
options.conveys: Playful editorial energy, tangible real subjects.
options.vs: Masked photography keeps the photo's rectangle or shape but crops it; cutouts remove the background along the subject's edge.
options.prompt: Use background-removed PNG/WebP cutouts of the subjects on flat brand-color backgrounds; optionally add a 6-10px white sticker outline and a hard or soft drop shadow; animate cutouts as rigid objects (translate, rotate plus/minus 6deg, scale settle).

options.what: Photos are cropped into designed shapes (arches, circles, type, blobs) as part of the layout.
options.looks: Arches, pills and circles containing photos; photos inside giant type.
options.motion: Mask shapes open, morph and rearrange; the image scales slowly inside.
options.use: Editorial and fashion, hospitality, wellness brands, landing-page heroes.
options.conveys: Designed elegance, editorial curation.
options.vs: Photo cutouts follow the subject's edge; masked photography imposes a graphic shape.
options.prompt: Crop photos into consistent graphic shapes (arch via border-radius 999px 999px 0 0, circles, pills) with overflow hidden; reveal by animating the clip-path open while the image inside scales from 1.15 to 1 over the same duration.

options.what: A still photo is separated into depth layers that move at different speeds, creating a 2.5D camera move.
options.looks: Foreground subject drifting against a slower background; subtle depth in a still image.
options.motion: Layers translate or scale at different rates (foreground faster) in a slow camera move.
options.use: Documentary, history, brand stories, archival material.
options.conveys: Immersion, memory brought to life.
options.vs: Ken Burns moves the camera across a flat photo; parallax separates the photo into layers with differential motion.
options.prompt: Split the photo into 2-4 layers (background plate, midground, cut-out foreground subject); run a slow camera move over 4-8s where the foreground translates 3-4x further than the background and scales 1 to 1.08, background 1 to 1.02.

options.what: A slow pan and zoom across a flat still image, named after the documentary filmmaker who popularized it.
options.looks: A still photo slowly pushing in or drifting across a detail.
options.motion: Slow scale (1 to 1.1-1.2) and translate over 4-10s with a gentle ease or linear.
options.use: Documentary, slideshows, testimonials, brand histories.
options.conveys: Reflection, narrative, gentle movement in stillness.
options.vs: Parallax photography has multiple depth layers; Ken Burns moves across one flat image.
options.prompt: Animate each still with a push or pan that goes somewhere: scale 1 to 1.15-1.25 and translate 4-8% toward the subject over 1.5-3 s with power2.inOut, then cut on the move (at least 4% a second: a slower drift is a creep that shimmers fine detail), never reversing direction within a shot.

options.what: Hand-drawn marks, scribbles, arrows and characters animated over photography.
options.looks: Marker circles, arrows, underlines, stars and doodle characters drawn over real photos.
options.motion: Strokes draw on with stroke-dashoffset, boil slightly, and interact with the subject.
options.use: Social content, creator brands, playful explainers, education.
options.conveys: Personality, humor, a human voice over reality.
options.vs: Video with tracked graphics sticks marks to moving points; photo + doodle is usually on stills or locked shots.
options.prompt: Draw hand-made SVG strokes (3-6px marker, round caps, slightly irregular paths) over the photo with stroke-dashoffset in 300-600ms each: circles around the subject, arrows to details, underlines; add a 3-frame line boil so the marks feel drawn.

options.what: Photography and type composed as one image, with type interacting with the subject (behind, around, cropped).
options.looks: Headline set behind a subject's head (depth sandwich), type wrapped around a figure, oversized letters cropped by the image.
options.motion: Type slides behind the subject, masks open, image and type move with parallax.
options.use: Editorial, fashion, campaign, sports and music posters in motion.
options.conveys: Editorial sophistication, integration of message and image.
options.vs: Full-bleed footage with overlaid text simply stacks text over image; photo + typography integrates them spatially.
options.prompt: Layer background plate, headline, then a cut-out of the subject on top so the type sits behind the subject; animate the headline sliding or revealing from behind the subject's silhouette while the photo pushes in 1 to 1.05.

options.what: Photography combined with 3D rendered objects or 3D-feeling graphics in the same scene.
options.looks: Glossy 3D objects sitting on real surfaces or floating in photographic environments with matched lighting.
options.motion: 3D objects rotate or float within the photo; camera moves respect the photo's perspective.
options.use: Product marketing, tech and consumer campaigns, surreal brand visuals.
options.conveys: Imagination grounded in reality, product magic.
options.vs: Photoreal CGI is fully rendered; photo + 3D mixes real photography with rendered or pseudo-3D elements.
options.prompt: Place pre-rendered 3D assets (PNG sequences, videos with alpha, or CSS 3D) into the photo matching its perspective and light direction, with a contact shadow (blurred ellipse at 30-40% black) below each object; animate objects floating or rotating subtly while the photo stays still or pushes slowly.

options.what: Graphics are attached to points in moving footage so they appear locked to objects in the scene.
options.looks: Labels, lines and shapes that follow a moving person, product or vehicle.
options.motion: Graphic positions follow tracking data frame by frame; callouts draw on and stay pinned.
options.use: Sports, product films, documentaries, tech demos, social explainers.
options.conveys: Precision, analysis, a world augmented by information.
options.vs: Tracked UI places interface elements in the scene; tracked graphics are labels and marks. Without tracking data, graphics are only approximately pinned.
options.prompt: Pin graphics to footage using exported tracking data (per-frame x/y keyframes converted to a GSAP keyframes array with ease none, matched to the video's frame rate); if no data exists, choose locked-off shots and keep graphics in static screen space. Callout lines draw from the tracked point to a label.

options.what: The content of a real device screen in footage is replaced with a recreated UI or screen recording.
options.looks: A person holding a phone or using a laptop, with crisp, on-brand UI on the screen.
options.motion: The inserted UI follows the device's movement via corner-pin tracking; UI interactions play inside.
options.use: Product films with lifestyle footage, app ads, testimonials.
options.conveys: Real people using the real product.
options.vs: Device mockups are rendered devices; screen replacement uses a real device in live-action footage.
options.prompt: Replace the device screen using four-corner pin data: apply a CSS matrix3d transform (computed from the tracked corners per frame) to the UI layer, add a subtle screen glare gradient and matching blur; for static shots, a single fixed matrix3d is sufficient.

options.what: Interface panels float in live-action space, anchored to real surfaces or objects.
options.looks: Translucent panels hovering beside a person or product, moving with the camera like AR.
options.motion: Panels follow camera motion with correct parallax; appear with scale and fade; interact with the scene.
options.use: AR/VR, AI assistant, smart home and wearable products; futuristic brand films.
options.conveys: The future, technology embedded in life.
options.vs: Tracked graphics are labels; tracked UI is functional interface in space. Floating screenshots float in graphic space, not in footage.
options.prompt: Anchor glassy UI panels (backdrop blur 16-24px, 1px white hairline at 30% alpha) to tracked points or planes in the footage, moving them with the tracking data plus slight parallax; reveal panels with a scale settle from 0.9 and a short light sweep.

options.what: Real product screenshots or recordings float as rounded, shadowed panels in graphic space, without devices.
options.looks: Rounded screenshots with soft shadows, sometimes tilted in perspective, layered over gradients.
options.motion: Panels slide in, tilt in 3D, stack and fan out; the camera pushes into details.
options.use: SaaS launch films, landing-page heroes, changelog videos, app store previews.
options.conveys: The real product, modern and clean.
options.vs: Device mockups wrap screenshots in hardware frames; floating screenshots are deviceless.
options.prompt: Present screenshots as panels with 16-24px radius, a 1px border at 8-10% ink and a layered soft shadow (0 30px 80px at 20-25% black); tilt in 3D (rotationX 10-20deg, rotationY -10deg, perspective 2000px) and untilt to flat as the camera pushes into the relevant region.

options.what: Product UI shown inside rendered hardware (phone, laptop, tablet, watch).
options.looks: Clean device frames, sometimes angled or in isometric arrangements, UI playing inside.
options.motion: Devices rotate into view, the camera orbits or pushes in, the UI animates inside.
options.use: App launches, app store videos, multi-platform products.
options.conveys: Real product on real platforms, tangibility.
options.vs: Floating screenshots skip the hardware; screen replacement uses real devices in footage.
options.prompt: Place the UI inside a device frame (PNG or SVG bezel with the screen area as an overflow-hidden container at the device's exact corner radius); animate the device as one unit (rotation, 3D tilt, push-in) while the UI animates inside; do not deform the device.

options.what: A small inset video (often a presenter or a detail) plays over a main view.
options.looks: A rounded or circular presenter bubble in a corner of a screen recording.
options.motion: The inset moves to avoid content, scales up for emphasis, docks to corners.
options.use: Tutorials, product demos with a presenter, reaction content, webinars.
options.conveys: Human guidance, presence, authenticity.
options.vs: Footage in UI is part of an interface; PiP is an editorial overlay layer above the main view.
options.prompt: Place the presenter footage in a 240-360px circle or rounded rectangle with a 3px border and soft shadow, docked 40px from a corner; move it to another corner (power3.inOut, 500ms) whenever content would be covered, and scale it up for emphasis moments.

options.what: Unpolished or observational real-world footage of people, places and work, used for authenticity.
options.looks: Handheld, natural light, real environments, interview framing, archival clips.
options.motion: Handheld camera motion; graphics are restrained (lower-thirds, captions, simple labels).
options.use: Customer stories, brand manifestos, recruitment, impact reports.
options.conveys: Truth, humanity, credibility.
options.vs: Cinematic product footage is controlled and lit; documentary footage is observational.
options.prompt: Keep documentary footage honest: minimal grade, no heavy effects; use restrained graphics only (a lower-third with name and role, a clean caption, a date or place label) entering with short mask reveals and leaving before the footage's key moments.

options.what: Controlled, lit footage of a physical product: macro details, slow sliders and orbits, dramatic light.
options.looks: Dark or seamless backgrounds, rim light, macro textures, slow-motion, reflections.
options.motion: Slow slider, orbit and push-in camera moves; high-speed shots; precise cuts to beats.
options.use: Hardware launches, consumer goods, automotive, luxury.
options.conveys: Premium craft, desire, precision.
options.vs: Documentary footage is observational and handheld; cinematic product footage is staged and lit.
options.prompt: Cut cinematic product shots to the music with minimal overlay: one line of type per shot in negative space, entering slowly (mask rise or blur-to-sharp if allowed), with graded shadows kept deep and a consistent color temperature across shots.
